description.value: The study investigated whether naturally varying testosterone levels in healthy young males are associated with behavioral performance and amygdala activation during explicit recognition of emotional facial expressions.

design.value: A cross-sectional within-subject functional MRI study of 21 right-handed healthy young males performing an event-related explicit emotion recognition task, with behavioral and amygdala responses correlated across participants with blood testosterone concentration.

description.value: Blood samples were taken on the day of fMRI measurements; testosterone was measured using an electrochemiluminescence-immunoassay.
The German version was used to exclude the presence of psychiatric disorders according to DSM IV.
Tasks engaging nonverbal intelligence, cognitive flexibility, visual learning and memory.

source_definition.value: anger, disgust, fear, happiness, sadness and neutral expressions
Blood testosterone levels measured on the day of fMRI measurements.

association_direction.value: positive association with amygdala response; negative association with reaction time to fearful male faces

description.value: Twenty-one right-handed healthy males aged 21–33 years; all participants were students and had no hormone treatment.

exclusion_criteria.value: psychiatric disorders according to DSM IV

recruitment_method.value: recruited by advertisements at the University of Vienna and the Medical University of Vienna, Austria

clinical_characteristics.value: All subjects performed above average according to norms on several neuropsychological tasks. No subject was alexithym.

medication_status.value: only males without any hormone treatment were included; all participants had a negative drug screening

education_summary.value: all students; mean education 17.9 years, S.D. = 3.2

task_description.value: Subjects viewed 72 color photographs of facial expressions portraying anger, disgust, fear, happiness, sadness and neutral expressions, and chose the correct emotion from two verbal possibilities by pressing the corresponding button.

presentation_software.value: Presentation software package (Neurobehavioral Systems Inc., Albany, CA, USA)

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to choose the correct emotion from two verbal possibilities presented on the left and right of the image, by pressing the corresponding button of a response box using the right hand.

stimuli.value: 72 color photographs of facial expressions portraying an equal number of the five basic emotions (anger, disgust, fear, happiness and sadness) as well as neutral expressions.

instrument.value: 3 Tesla Medspec whole-body scanner (Bruker Biospin, Ettlingen, Germany)

description.value: Gradient-recalled echo-planar imaging with 10 oblique axial slices centered on the amygdala employing asymmetric k-space sampling; FOV = 25 cm × 21 cm, matrix size 128 × 91, slice thickness 2 mm, slice gap 0.5 mm, TR = 1000 ms, TE = 31 ms.
Functional images were slice timing corrected, realigned to the mean image, normalized into standardized stereotactic space, and spatially smoothed.

steps.value: spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel with a full-width-at-half-maximum of 9 mm

model_type.value: event-related design; each stimulus was modelled with a separate regressor

hrf_model.value: canonical hemodynamic response function and its temporal derivative

model_settings.value: Regressors of each valence were pooled to assess brain responses to each emotion, leaving a minimum of 12 stimuli per category for statistical analysis. Contrast images from all subjects were included in a second level random effects analysis.

level.value: individual and group level; second level random effects analysis

estimator.value: two-way ANOVA with emotion and gender of poser as within-subject factors; three-way repeated-measures ANOVA for the ROI analysis; Pearson correlations for testosterone associations
